notes.summary: Partial P15.1 theorem: for a supplied holomorphic fibration and pullback Kähler class, bounded unnormalized relative base energy is independent of all calibrated Kähler directions, including non-descending bounded approximants with uniform convergence and no epsilon-relative rate. Singular fibres are included; the original general atom remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: Let pi:X->B be surjective between connected smooth compact Kähler manifolds, n>nu>=1, theta=pi*beta, m=n-nu, K=binom(n,nu), and V=int_B beta^nu. The degree-zero current pi_*(omega^m) is a positive constant c. For bounded beta-psh phi and any bounded (theta+epsilon omega_epsilon)-psh u_epsilon uniformly converging to pi*phi, with omega_epsilon smoothly converging to any Kähler form, E_(theta+epsilon omega_epsilon)(u_epsilon)/(K c_epsilon epsilon^m) tends to the raw E_beta(phi). The error is O(delta_epsilon)+O(epsilon), without delta_epsilon=o(epsilon). Relative cocycles, shifts by bV, monotonicity, concavity, bounded affine variations, continuous C1 uniform-path first variations, and compensating base-reference changes are proved. Exact bounded-current projection holds through critical values. No unbounded P-type, E1 completion, canonical carrier, arbitrary degenerate path, or solution for a general pseudoeffective zero-volume class is claimed. The proof is an unverified author draft with explicit standard foundations, not an independently certified theorem.
notes.text:
This is partial progress on P15.1, not a complete solution of the original general pseudoeffective zero-volume problem. The authoritative full proof is P15.1-argument.md; the standalone full-proof paper is P15.1-partial.tex and its twice-compiled P15.1-partial.pdf. The operator proposal and earlier comparison-paper verdicts are not proof premises. No companion-task output was used.

Exact setting and claim. Use ddc=i/(2pi) partial barpartial and dc=i/(4pi)(barpartial-partial). Let pi:X->B be a supplied surjective holomorphic map between connected smooth compact Kähler manifolds of dimensions n and nu, 1<=nu<n, with m=n-nu. Neither smooth fibres, flatness, equidimensionality, nor a product is assumed. Fix a Kähler form beta on B, theta=pi*beta, V=int_B beta^nu, K=binom(n,nu). For bounded beta-psh phi let U=phi composed with pi and C_phi=beta+ddc phi. Bounded means everywhere finite bounded quasi-psh representatives; convergence is the pointwise uniform norm, not an essential supremum.

For any Kähler omega, pi_*(omega^m)=c_omega is a positive constant. More generally take Kähler omega_epsilon converging smoothly to any Kähler omega_0, and write c_epsilon=pi_*(omega_epsilon^m), q_epsilon=theta+epsilon omega_epsilon, s_epsilon=K c_epsilon epsilon^m. For ANY bounded q_epsilon-psh u_epsilon with delta_epsilon=||u_epsilon-U||_infinity->0, the unnormalized energy E_q(v)=(1/(d+1)) sum_(j=0)^d int_Y v(q+ddc v)^j q^(d-j) satisfies E_q_epsilon(u_epsilon)/s_epsilon -> E_beta(phi). No descent of u_epsilon or epsilon-relative rate is assumed. If bounded v_epsilon uniformly approximates pi*psi under the same backgrounds, the calibrated relative energies converge to R_beta(phi,psi), where R_q(v,w)=(1/(d+1)) sum_j int_Y(v-w)T_v^j T_w^(d-j). One may replace c_epsilon by c_omega_0. A supporting energy-variation estimate proves pi_*((q_epsilon+ddc u_epsilon)^n)/s_epsilon -> C_phi^nu weakly on B, with raw mass V. This does not claim to solve the general P15.2 target.

Exact imported foundations. Locally bounded psh potentials define closed positive symmetric Bedford--Taylor products recursively by ddc(p S); simultaneous local decreasing smooth psh regularizations yield weak convergence of mixed products. Citation: Bedford and Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Math.149 (1982), 1-40, Section2; their Fine topology, Shilov boundary, and (ddc)^n, J. Funct. Anal.72 (1987),225-251; bounded construction also BEGZ arXiv:0812.3674v2 LF175-188, and local continuity application LF668-679. Multilinearity here follows by smooth local approximation and finite expansion; no unbounded multilinearity assertion is borrowed. The bounded special case of BEGZ Theorem1.14/Lemma1.15 states: on a compact Kähler manifold, for closed positive bidimension(1,1) Theta and bounded quasi-psh differences a,b, int a ddc b Theta = int b ddc a Theta = -int db dc a Theta; the signed integrals are finite and da dc a Theta is a finite positive measure. Citation: Boucksom, Eyssidieux, Guedj, Zeriahi, Monge-Ampère equations in big cohomology classes, Acta Math.205 (2010),199-262; primary arXiv:0812.3674v2 LF626-762. Every application below uses A=empty, globally bounded quasi-psh differences, and a closed positive mixed BT current of the required bidimension. The standard nef convention is that nef positive products equal cup products, volume is the top product, and nef numerical dimension is max{k:int alpha^k kappa^(n-k)>0}; BEGZ Definition1.17 and discussion, LF810-840. These apply because theta is smooth semipositive and all positive perturbations are Kähler. Stokes for currents and Sard's smooth critical-value theorem are also used; Sard, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.48 (1942),883-890. All new projection, mass, estimate, and energy applications are derived next.

Proof of the transverse constant and numerical data. Proper holomorphic pushforward of the closed positive (m,m) form omega^m is closed positive of degree zero. A scalar distribution with zero derivatives is constant: local convolution gives functions with zero gradient, and overlap and connectedness give one constant. Thus it is c on all B, with no term supported at critical values. Surjectivity and Sard give a full-rank open set. Consequently int_X theta^nu omega^m>0, and pairing the pushforward with beta^nu gives c=(int_X theta^nu omega^m)/V>0. At any regular value ordinary submersion-coordinate fibre integration gives c=int_(pi^-1(b)) omega^m, summed over disconnected components. Stokes gives representative independence in a fixed auxiliary class; c_(t omega)=t^m c_omega, so c is not class independent. Since theta^(nu+1)=0 and the nu-th mixed intersection is positive, alpha=[theta] is nef, psef, volume zero, and numerical dimension nu. Its perturbative volume is sum_(k=0)^nu binom(n,k) epsilon^(n-k) int_X theta^k omega^(n-k), hence K c V epsilon^m+O(epsilon^(m+1)). Smooth auxiliary convergence makes all coefficients bounded and c_epsilon->c_omega_0>0.

Proof of bounded projection through singular fibres. On base charts write each positive bounded-potential factor C_i=ddc p_i with p_i locally bounded psh. The compositions p_i composed with pi are locally bounded psh; their BT products are the defined pullback products. Local smooth decreasing psh approximations on the base pull back and converge in BT sense. Products of more than nu base factors vanish at the smooth levels by dimension, hence at the limit on all X. For k<=nu, set P_0=omega^m and P_r=ddc((p_r composed with pi)P_(r-1)). Bounded Borel multiplication of order-zero currents gives pi_*((g composed with pi)S)=g pi_*S: this follows by integrating coefficient measures against pulled-back test forms. Proper holomorphic pushforward commutes with ddc. Induction therefore gives pi_*P_r=ddc(p_r pi_*P_(r-1))=c C_r...C_1. This proves pi_*(pi*C_1...pi*C_k omega^m)=c C_1...C_k on every chart, including critical values. It is not a projection theorem for arbitrary singular currents. In particular, for a+b=nu and any bounded Borel g, int_X(g composed with pi)H^a theta^b omega^m=c int_B g C_phi^a beta^b, where H=theta+ddc U. Taking g=phi justifies the discontinuously weighted energy term exactly, without testing weak convergence against phi.

Mixed mass identity. Replacing one bounded-potential current q_i+ddc w_i by q_i changes a mixed product by the globally exact current ddc(w_i S), with S the remaining closed mixed product. Boundedness makes w_i S order zero; local BT recursion verifies the identity and patches globally. Stokes against complementary closed smooth forms gives the ordinary cup-product mixed masses. This includes semipositive theta and all mixed currents below.

Proof of all bounded energy laws. For a Kähler background q on a compact d-fold, all mixed masses equal V_q=int q^d, so E_q(0)=0 and E_q(v+b)=E_q(v)+b V_q. Along a bounded affine segment v_t=(1-t)w+tv with h=v-w, multilinearity makes the energy a finite polynomial. Differentiate it and apply bounded IBP with a=v_t, b=h, Theta=T_v_t^(j-1) q^(d-j). The second contribution becomes j int h(T_v_t-q)T_v_t^(j-1)q^(d-j). The sum telescopes to dE_q(v_t)/dt=int h T_v_t^d, with one-sided endpoint derivatives. Integrating the segment and using int_0^1 binom(d,j)t^j(1-t)^(d-j)dt=1/(d+1) yields E_q(v)-E_q(w)=R_q(v,w). Thus R_q(v,w)+R_q(w,z)=R_q(v,z). Ordered endpoints give monotonicity. Comparing v with w plus or minus ||v-w|| gives |E_q(v)-E_q(w)|<=V_q||v-w||. Differentiating again and using IBP with a=b=h and Theta=T_v_t^(d-1) gives d^2E/dt^2=-d int dh dc h T_v_t^(d-1)<=0, proving concavity, with the finite positive BT gradient-square measure.

The additional first-variation scope is a C1 path t->v_t in the Banach space C(Y) with the uniform norm, every v_t q-psh. For uniform a_l->a, telescoping mixed products and testing with smooth f, -C_f q<=ddc f<=C_f q, gives |int f(T_a_l^j T_a^(d-j)-T_a^d)|<=j C_f V_q||a_l-a||. Equal masses and smooth approximation give weak convergence on continuous tests. Divide the relative energy formula for v_(t+h),v_t by h: the velocities converge uniformly to the continuous dot v_t and the mixed measures converge weakly, yielding dE_q(v_t)/dt=int dot v_t T_v_t^d. There is no claimed first variation for arbitrary discontinuous velocities or arbitrary perturbative time paths; the stated nonsmooth second variation is for affine segments only.

Leading energy and no-rate stability. In E_q_epsilon(U), expand (H+epsilon omega_epsilon)^j(theta+epsilon omega_epsilon)^(n-j). Only terms with a+b<=nu horizontal factors survive. At power epsilon^m the coefficient multiplying int U H^a theta^(nu-a) omega_epsilon^m is (1/(n+1)) sum_j binom(j,a)binom(n-j,nu-a)=K/(nu+1). Count (nu+1)-element subsets of {1,...,n+1} by their (a+1)-st element to prove this identity. Exact weighted projection gives E_q_epsilon(U)=s_epsilon E_beta(phi)+O(||phi|| epsilon^(m+1)). For all remaining finitely many terms, their absolute integrals are bounded by ||phi|| int_X theta^(a+b)omega_epsilon^(n-a-b), by the positive mixed mass identity. The energy Lipschitz bound gives |E_q_epsilon(u_epsilon)-E_q_epsilon(U)|<=delta_epsilon int q_epsilon^n. Divide by s_epsilon: the total error is at most delta_epsilon(V+O(epsilon))+O(||phi||epsilon). This proves the energy limit, and applying it twice proves the relative limit. It removes the entire auxiliary class after its own c calibration, not merely its representative. An admissible non-descending example with slower convergence is u_epsilon=sqrt(epsilon) pi*f+epsilon zeta at phi=0, where f is smooth nonconstant and zeta is a sufficiently small smooth function varying on a regular fibre with omega+ddc zeta>0. Then beta+sqrt(epsilon)ddc f>0 for small epsilon, and the uniform error has order sqrt(epsilon).

Supporting measure estimate. Set A=q_epsilon+ddc u_epsilon and D=H+epsilon omega_epsilon. Factor A^n-D^n=ddc(u_epsilon-U) sum_(j=0)^(n-1) A^j D^(n-1-j). For smooth real f on B, bound plus/minus pi*ddc f by C_f theta. Bounded IBP against F=f composed with pi gives |int F(A^n-D^n)|<=n C_f delta_epsilon I_epsilon, where every mixed theta integral equals I_epsilon=int theta q_epsilon^(n-1). Its leading term is binom(n-1,nu-1)c_epsilon V epsilon^m, so I_epsilon/s_epsilon=(nu/n)V+O(epsilon). The scaled difference is O_f(delta_epsilon), with no epsilon-relative rate. The exact pullback expansion is pi_*D^n=s_epsilon C_phi^nu+sum_(k=0)^(nu-1) binom(n,k)epsilon^(n-k) pi_*(H^k omega_epsilon^(n-k)). Its positive remainder has mass O(epsilon^(m+1)), hence calibrated total variation O(epsilon). The scaled A measures have masses V+O(epsilon); smooth test approximation proves weak convergence on continuous tests. Total variation convergence for arbitrary non-descending A is not asserted.

Reference and path scopes. Fixed arbitrary Kähler forms in any classes each yield the identical base limit using their own c. For smoothly convergent Kähler families, coefficients are uniformly bounded and c stays away from zero; using instantaneous c_epsilon or the limiting c is equivalent. Reparameterization is harmless. No arbitrary degenerate auxiliary path is claimed. For beta'=beta+ddc h Kähler, h smooth real, compensate phi'=phi-h and psi'=psi-h. The represented currents and potential difference are unchanged, so R_beta'(phi-h,psi-h)=R_beta(phi,psi). Since h is beta-psh, E_beta'(phi-h)=E_beta(phi)-E_beta(h). The mass V is unchanged. At positive epsilon, H_h=pi*h, q'_epsilon=q_epsilon+ddc H_h, u'_epsilon=u_epsilon-H_h give exactly E_q'_epsilon(u'_epsilon)=E_q_epsilon(u_epsilon)-E_q_epsilon(H_h). Thus the reference correction survives the limit, and a common represented reference current gives an invariant relative energy. The needed form of the compact Kähler ddc lemma says every exact real smooth closed (1,1) form is ddc of a smooth real function; Deligne, Griffiths, Morgan, Sullivan, Invent. Math.29 (1975),245-274. Its applicability is the compact Kähler base; the formulas already assume the exhibited h.

Optional continuous descent. If fibres are connected and W is continuous theta-psh, W=pi*phi for a unique continuous beta-psh phi. The additional imported standard foundation is analytic resolution: each compact irreducible reduced complex analytic space has a proper surjective resolution by a smooth connected compact complex manifold, isomorphic over a dense nonsingular open set; Bierstone and Milman, Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero by blowing up the maximum strata of a local invariant, Invent. Math.128 (1997),207-302, Main Theorem in the complex analytic category. Apply it to every reduced irreducible fibre component. Pullback of W+rho composed with pi, where beta=ddc rho locally, restricts to a psh function differing from W by a constant on the resolution. The compact smooth psh maximum principle makes it constant. Constants match on intersecting components, and connectedness of the finite component graph makes W fibrewise constant, including higher-dimensional singular components. A compact-to-Hausdorff continuous surjection is a quotient map, hence phi is continuous. Finally pi_*((theta+ddc W)omega^m)=c(beta+ddc phi) is positive, so beta+ddc phi>=0. Local convolution of this continuous function plus rho and the limiting submean inequalities make it psh. This additional resolution foundation is not needed for the main supplied-pullback theorem.

Scope comparison and limitations. The carrier is the supplied B of dimension nu; the base reference beta and its potential zero fix raw mass V>0 and E_beta(0)=0. Constants shift energy by bV. All potentials treated have bounded/minimal singularity type relative to these smooth backgrounds. The positive transverse s_epsilon is not division by vol(alpha)=0; the full leading volume coefficient is K c V, so dividing by it would instead normalize away V. No reconstruction from I-equivalence is asserted. This substantially extends the old smooth fixed-auxiliary-class calculation, but the fibration and pullback Kähler hypothesis are additional. There is no canonical carrier or globally minimal reference scale for arbitrary classes, no independence on changing pi, no E1 completion, no prescribed unbounded P-type, and no arbitrary degenerate direction theorem. Original P15.1 remains open. This is an unverified author proof with precisely stated standard foundations, not an independent mathematical verdict.
